subject: Estrogen-only therapy in later life linked to fewer Alzheimer's signs in the brain
script: From Agewell Brief: Estrogen-only therapy in later life linked to fewer Alzheimer's signs in the brain. A large observational study finds that women who used estrogen-only hormone therapy after age 70 had lower odds of dementia and less Alzheimer's pathology at autopsy. The findings revive a decades-old biophysical question: can a steroid hormone reshape the aging brain's molecular landscape? Read the full source-linked dispatch and primary study caveats at AgewellBrief.com.
